html:
Fixed

  • Speech from a TtsProvider could crackle and skip in a render with several jobs: every job called the provider for a line that was not cached yet and wrote the same tts/ file at once, splicing two takes into one WAV. Now one process speaks the line and the others wait for its cache entry, which is written whole (WAV first, then the JSON). Delete the tts/ files of a line that sounds broken and render again.
  • oxframe dev: reloading the page while the video played showed it paused while frames kept moving, with no sound. A new page now stops playback (and the editor, 0.1.7, asks for that itself).
  • A trimmed sound (or a recording that does not start at zero) no longer clicks: every clip fades in and out over 2 ms.

Fixed

  • The preview (oxframe dev, oxframe present) read --cpu as "draw on the GPU". It now takes --gpu for vello, as render does; the CPU stays the default and --cpu is still accepted.
  • Skills: formulas are Math::new (feature math), not "not yet"; oxframe-check no longer lists input_cycle (gone since 0.21) and gives bounds in scene units, as the report has them; a snapshot is 960×540 unless --size says otherwise; the voiceover skill covers recorded voice-overs; the oxframe mcp tool list is complete.

Added

  • The browser build of a project can run the checks: the wasm module exports check (the report and the storyboard PNG), inspect and a frame as PNG. The remote MCP server at mcp.oxframe.dev uses them to check a scene without a local install.

Added

  • Voice-overs you recorded yourself: voice("…").recording("vo/intro.wav") plays the file instead of calling a speech provider, and the line lasts as long as the file. oxframe transcribe vo/intro.wav (oxframe-cli) times its words with whisper.cpp on your machine and writes vo/intro.words.json, so line.at_word("…") and .caption() follow the recording. Without that file the words are spread over its length.

Fixed

  • Projects on oxframe 0.23.0–0.23.4 build again. 0.23.5 added a field to oxframe_export::MixRequest, and since a project's oxframe-export resolves to the newest 0.23.x, the older oxframe stopped compiling. The target loudness is now an argument: oxframe_export::mix_with_loudness. 0.23.5 is yanked; oxframe upgrade moves a project to 0.23.6.

Added

  • No ffmpeg installed? oxframe render downloads a static build once into the oxframe cache and uses it (oxframe-cli); oxframe ffmpeg does it ahead of time.
  • Six more blocks for oxframe add (oxframe-cli), 24 in all: metric-row, key-combo, steps, social-post, split-screen and search-bar.
  • voice("…").caption(): the line is shown at the bottom of the frame while it is spoken, up to seven words at a time, each part on screen while its words are said (word timings from the provider, or the estimate). Captions burned into the video, for feeds that play muted.
  • oxframe check: most issues carry fix, the change that clears them with the numbers worked out — move by dx/dy pixels, shrink to a size, a text color (the same hue, lightened or darkened) and the contrast it reaches, widen by pixels or a font_scale, hold or slow in seconds. The hints say the same in words ("Move it 140 px to the left"). lint::Fix in Rust.
  • Project::loudness, say at -14 LUFS: the rendered sound (music, voice and effects) is brought to that integrated loudness (EBU R128) before the -1 dBFS limiter, so a video plays as loud as others on YouTube or in a feed. render prints the loudness of every mix; oxframe_export::loudness measures one.
  • GIF export: render --format gif (or --out demo.gif) writes a looping GIF with one palette for the whole clip and an ordered dither that does not shimmer. It is 720 pixels wide and 15 fps unless --size and --fps say otherwise; frames are taken from the project's rate, so only the frames the GIF shows are rendered. No sound. Format::Gif in oxframe-export.

Added

  • oxframe mcp --dir (oxframe-cli): serve the project at a given path, not the current directory, for MCP clients that start servers elsewhere.

Fixed

  • oxframe check no longer reports dead_time while a Video plays: the clip frame it shows counts as change (inspect lists it as the frame param). A paused or finished clip still counts as a still shot.

Added

  • Six more blocks for oxframe add (oxframe-cli): feature-grid, checklist, comparison, chat-messages, pull-request and countdown, eighteen in all, every one passing oxframe check.
  • The agent skill: a request to explain or show something means a scene, not an answer in chat; hints for the compile errors seen most in the 0.23.2 agent eval. No SDK code changed.

Added

  • oxframe publish (oxframe-cli): renders the project, or takes an MP4, uploads it to oxframe.dev and prints a link with a player that unfolds as a video in Discord and Slack. Up to 30 s and 16 MB (a larger render is re-encoded at 720p); kept for 30 days. --title names the page. No SDK code changed; the agent skill knows the command.

Added

  • Custom WGSL shaders (Shader::source, Shader::file, and their Input::frame() and Input::node inputs) paint in the browser playground too: the CPU interpreter is built for wasm. A 1080p frame takes about 0.3 s there; playback skips frames to keep time. The browser bundle grows by about 360 KB gzipped.

Added

  • Components convert to Node (From<X> and From<&X>): Axes, Callout, CodeExplainer, FlowDiagram, LowerThird, ChapterMarker, Matrix, Table, TitleCard, EndCard, BulletList go wherever a node does, e.g. caption.next_to(&end_card, Side::Bottom).
  • Txt::font_size, Txt::weight and Code::font_size take integers too: .font_size(64).
  • .scale(..) on a builder takes one number, a pair or a Vec2: .scale(1.5), .scale((2.0, 0.5)), .scale(2).
  • oxframe check: low_contrast reads the pixels behind text that lies over a shader, an image, a video, Custom, particles or 3D. The frame is drawn without text and the ratio is the median over the text's box; it must last 0.5 s to count, so something moving past a label is not reported. Text over plain fills is judged as before.
  • A custom WGSL shade (Shader::source, Shader::file) is painted, not only checked: an interpreter over naga's IR runs it on the CPU, a tile of pixels at a time, with the same bytes on every OS (about 0.13 s for a 1080p frame in a release build). Textures, samplers and derivatives are a shader_error. The playground does not paint it.
  • Inputs of a custom shader: .input("photo", Input::file("photo.png")) (or Input::image(include_bytes!(..))) is read in WGSL with sample_photo(uv). With .input("scene", Input::frame()) the shader reads what was drawn before it and is painted over it inside its box, e.g. sample_scene(i.screen / ox.resolution). Calling sample_x with no input x is a shader_error that says how to add it.
  • Shader::size(width, height), like width and height together.
  • Example magnifier: a lens written in WGSL that reads the frame.
  • .offscreen() on any node: it is drawn only for a shader that reads it with Input::node(handle) (sample_<name>(uv), uv across the node's box), never on screen, and check skips it.

Changed

  • lens_drops, node.effect(..) and a frame-reading shader work inside a group with opacity below 1, a blur, a clip, a blend, a shadow or another effect. The group is drawn in parts on its own, then faded or blurred as a whole; a shader in it reads what the group drew before it. check no longer reports input_cycle.

Fixed

  • check no longer reports covers_text for a custom shader that reads the frame (Input::frame()): the text shows through it, as under lens_drops. InspectNode has a reads_frame field.
  • A vector's label (axes.vector(..).label("i")) sits off to the side of the tip, so a vector along an axis no longer puts its label on the axis line.

Breaking

  • Signal::set takes impl Into<T>, like Signal::to, so text.set("Done") and fill.set(Accent) work. A value converted with a bare .into() no longer infers its type: drop the .into(). Before: m.cell(0, 1).text().set("7".into()); → after: m.cell(0, 1).text().set("7");
  • Node::scale() returns ScaleSignal, a Signal<Vec2> (it derefs to one) whose to and set also take one number for both axes: node.scale().to(1.2, 0.3). Code that names the type changes. Before: let s: Signal<Vec2> = node.scale(); → after: let s: Signal<Vec2> = node.scale().signal(); (or .into()).
  • lint::Sample has a contrast field (measured contrast per text node). Before: Sample { time, nodes } → after: Sample { time, nodes, contrast: Vec::new() }.
  • Input is no longer Copy (it can hold an image); Input::name takes &self. Clone it where it was copied.
  • InspectNode has a reads_frame field; add reads_frame: false where you build one.

Added

  • oxframe check --against (a directory) compares this check's frames with an earlier oxframe check --frames output: each frame that changed gets a share of changed pixels and diff/<time>.png, the frame dimmed with the changed pixels in red; report.json gets a comparison (changed, the same, added, removed). Check whether an edit changed only what it meant to.
  • oxframe check reports where things move: report.json gets motion, each node that travels with its file:line, the stretches of time it moves visibly (moves, its keyframes), where it starts and ends, and the length of its path; a child that only rides with its parent is left out. out/check/trajectories/<scene>.png draws the paths on the scene's last frame, numbered as in motion.
  • The storyboard shows both sides of a hard cut between scenes: the last frame of a scene and the first of the next.
  • Image::decode_png.
  • The quickstart example: install, oxframe init and oxframe render in a terminal, then the rendered scene plays. It is the animation in the README's quickstart (scripts/readme-gif.sh makes the GIF).

Tested

  • CPU frames are byte-for-byte the same on Linux (x86_64 and arm64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows: CI renders ten examples on each and compares the hashes.

Changed

  • Frames are drawn on the CPU (tiny-skia) by default, in oxframe render and in the preview of oxframe dev and oxframe present. The CPU is faster than the GPU on every scene of the benchmark, and it is the byte-for-byte deterministic renderer. --gpu opts into vello. --cpu is still accepted and wins over --gpu, so existing commands keep working. Before → after: oxframe render drew on the GPU and now draws on the CPU; oxframe render --gpu draws on the GPU as the default used to.

Added

  • oxframe check writes a crop for each issue on a node: out/check/issues/<n>-<rule>.png, the part of the frame around the node at full resolution with the node outlined in red (up to 24 per check). In report.json such an issue has bounds, the node's rect at the start of the issue in scene units (as in inspect), and crop, the path relative to out/check/. A node wholly outside the frame gets the strip along the edge it is past.
  • Math::new("e^(i pi) + 1 = 0"): formulas set by Typst, behind the new math feature (crate oxframe-math). .size(px) is the font size, as for Txt; .display() sets the formula on its own line (limits above and below, full-size fractions); .color(..) and the color() signal paint every glyph; paths() are the glyphs and rules in reading order, for stagger. The font (New Computer Modern Math) is bundled, so no TeX is needed. The feature adds the Typst compiler and a 1.4 MB font, so the browser playground does not have it; the formulas example runs with cargo run -p oxframe-examples --features math --bin formulas -- preview.
  • docs.rs now documents the icons, 3d, math and unstable-node-api features.
  • CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md; plugins for Cursor and Codex with the same skills and oxframe mcp as the Claude Code one; a README quickstart from install to the first render.

Faster

  • The CPU renderer keeps a layer's blurred drop shadow across frames while the layer does not change, instead of blurring it again on every frame. A fading or blurred group keeps its cached pixels too. Output is unchanged.

Added

  • The one_shot example: the oxframe promo video, one scene and one camera with no cuts, with its voice committed so it renders without a key. Its source is the code behind the video on oxframe.dev and X.

Fixed

  • oxframe dev: after a rebuild while the video plays, the picture and the sound go on together from the frame they were on. The editor used to start the sound from the beginning over a still picture.

Fixed

  • oxframe check reported text_overflow for text in a row of a Layout nested in another one: a row that draws nothing itself was placed as if there were no layout. oxframe inspect now gives every node the box it is drawn in.
  • oxframe check reported dead_time while text was written on word by word, while a glow changed and while a sea from shaders::waves() moved. They count as change now; oxframe inspect lists how much of a node is drawn and its glow among its params.

Changed

  • The release example: each section's heading in its color, the changes written on word by word with a short halo, and a calm sea along the bottom. release-video-action 1.3 makes its videos the same way.

Fixed

  • TitleCard and EndCard wrap a long title or second line inside the card, and the card grows to hold it. A long line used to run past the card's edges, which release videos with long notes showed.
  • Centered and end-aligned text with a max_width was drawn beside its own box when it was narrower than max_width (a single short line, say). It now sits inside the box, so placing it and oxframe check see where it really is.

Added

  • Every issue in report.json has docs: the link to its rule on https://oxframe.dev/docs/check-rules, with what the rule reports and how to fix it (Issue::docs).
  • The showreel example: scenes from other examples between a title and an end card, the reel on oxframe.dev.

Fixed

  • check reported too_fast at a cut between two scenes when the first node of each had the same id: node ids start again in every scene, and a move is now only a node added at the same place.

Parallel rendering.

Added

  • render --jobs 4 renders a video in 2-second segments, several at once, each in its own process; the segments are joined without re-encoding and the soundtrack is added once. The default is one job per core, at most eight. A PNG sequence is split the same way.
  • The file does not depend on the number of jobs: --jobs 1 and --jobs 8 write the same bytes. A 7-second 3D scene renders 2.7 times faster on 8 cores.
  • oxframe_export::concat joins segments encoded with the same settings.

Changed

  • A video longer than two seconds now has a key frame every two seconds (where the segments meet), so files are a little larger than before.

3D scenes inside 2D ones, behind the 3d feature.

Added

  • Scene3d is a world of meshes: Mesh::cube(), Mesh::sphere(), Mesh::plane(), Mesh::cylinder(), Mesh::group() and models from a binary glTF (Mesh::glb_file). .color(), .metallic(), .roughness(), .emissive() and .opacity() set the material.
  • scene.add(mesh) returns an Object3d whose position, rotation, scale, color and opacity are signals, so .to() animates them; object.add(mesh) makes a child that moves with its parent.
  • scene.camera() (position, target, field of view) and scene.light(Light::directional(..)) or Light::point(..) are signals too; with no light, a default sunlight shades each face differently.
  • View3d::new(&scene).size(640.0, 400.0) shows the scene as a 2D node: position, opacity, effects, the 2D camera and layout work as for any node. view.projector() maps a 3D point into the view, so a 2D label follows a corner of a model.
  • The renderer is a software rasterizer with a depth buffer and 2 × 2 supersampling: the same scene gives the same pixels in a render, in check, in CI without a GPU and in the browser playground.
  • DrawCtx::image draws a picture from a node of your own.
  • The cube_3d example.

Presentations from the same scenes.

Added

  • slide_break().await marks a stop. A render plays straight through it; oxframe present (CLI 0.18.0) pauses there until the next key press. The last frame of every scene is a stop too.
  • notes("…") adds speaker notes for the part that ends at the next stop.
  • render --slides talk.pdf writes a PDF with the frame of every stop, one per page, without ffmpeg.
  • The timeline sent to the editor lists the stops.
  • The slides example.

Fixed

  • Rendering with --subtitles from oxframe render now works: the CLI passes the flag to the project (CLI 0.18.0).

Matrices, vectors and tables.

Added

  • Matrix::new([[1, 2], [3, 4]]) draws values in square brackets. Each cell is a Txt from cell(r, c), row(r) or column(c); row_frame, column_frame and cell_frame give hidden outlines to fade in. .cell_width(px) leaves room for longer values.
  • axes.vector(x, y) draws an arrow from the origin whose tip is two signals; v.to(x, y, seconds) moves it and .label("v") follows it.
  • axes.apply_matrix(m, seconds) maps the plane through a 2 × 2 matrix: a transformed grid is drawn over the original, and plots, series, vectors and placed nodes move with it. axes.matrix() is the Mat2 signal; Mat2::after multiplies and Mat2::det gives the determinant.
  • Table::new takes the column titles and .row(..) adds rows. insert_row, push_row and remove_row slide the other rows into place, sort_by_column and sort_by move every row to its sorted place, and table.row(i) is a TableRow with a background to highlight it.
  • Guide lesson 15, and the matrix_multiply, linear_map and table_sort examples.

Icons from Lucide, Tabler and Simple Icons, behind the icons feature.

Added

  • icon!("lucide:server") adds an icon by set and name: lucide:, tabler: (with -filled variants) and simple: for brand logos. Only the icons a project names are put into its binary. A name that does not exist fails to compile and lists the closest names.
  • .size(), .color() and .stroke_width() on the builder; the Icon handle has color() and stroke_width() as signals, Icon::paths for draw_on, and Icon::style (IconStyle::Stroke or IconStyle::Fill). The color defaults to the theme's text color.
  • Icon::from_svg makes the same node from a 24 by 24 SVG of your own.
  • FlowDiagram puts an icon at the start of a card with .icon(name, icon!(..)); flow.icon(name) returns its handle.
  • The architecture example.

Fixed

  • Creating GPU renderers on several threads at once could crash inside the Vulkan driver. Renderers now share one Vulkan, Metal or DX12 instance; a GL-only machine still gets one per renderer.

Video clips in a scene, behind the video feature.

Added

  • Video::new().file("assets/demo.mp4") shows a clip as a node, sized with .width(pct(70)) like an image, with .radius(24.0) corners, effects and the camera. demo.play(), demo.pause() and demo.seek(2.0) control it; demo.playback_rate() and demo.time() are signals, so demo.playback_rate().to(0.25, 0.5) slows it down.
  • The frame shown is a function of the scene's time, so a render and a seek show the same frame. Frames are decoded with ffmpeg and cached; WebM (VP9) and ProRes 4444 keep their alpha.
  • The clip's sound goes to the mixer while it plays at rate 1; .muted(true) leaves it out.
  • check reports video_unavailable when a clip cannot be opened.
  • The video example.

Fixed

  • The mixer read the first track of a file; for a video that is the picture. It now takes the first audio track.

Nodes of your own, behind the unstable-node-api feature.

Added

  • #[derive(Node)] on a struct that implements Draw makes it a node. Fields marked #[signal] get a setter on the builder (Gauge::new()) and a signal on the handle (GaugeHandle), so gauge.value().to(0.8, 1.0) animates them. Other fields are set once.
  • Draw::draw paints with the same DrawCtx as Custom, and Draw::size gives the box that layout, Camera::fit and check use. The node gets position, opacity, effects, flex properties and theme colors like any built-in one, and check names it by its type.
  • DrawCtx::arc strokes or fills an arc, for gauges and rings.
  • oxframe init --template node my-node makes a crate with a node, a demo scene and a reference test.
  • The gauge example.

Charts: axes, number lines, function plots and bars, all following animated ranges.

Added

  • Axes::new() is a plotting box with a grid, axes, ticks and labels. .x_range(-5.0..5.0) and .y_range(-2.0..2.0) set the data ranges, .width() and .height() the box, .no_grid() drops the grid. axes.x_range() is a signal of Interval, so axes.x_range().to(-10.0..10.0, 1.0) zooms; ticks stay on round steps and each label keeps its value while the range slides.
  • axes.plot(|x| x.sin()) draws a function as a Plot. It is sampled again every frame, finer where it bends, broken at jumps (no line across the gaps of tan) and cut at the box. .stroke(Accent) and .width(4.0) style it, .draw_on() draws it, and plot.to_fn(|x| x.cos(), 1.0) morphs it into another function.
  • axes.point_on(&plot, x) keeps a dot on the curve at a signal x. axes.c2p(x, y) gives the scene point of a data point, and axes.place(node, x, y) keeps a node there.
  • axes.bars([3.0, 7.5]) draws bars with their values above them; bars.value(0).to(9.0, 1.0) grows one, .labels(["a", "b"]) names them. axes.line_series(..) and axes.scatter(..) draw data points.
  • NumberLine::new(0.0..10.0) is a single axis with the same methods.
  • Guide lesson 14 (charts) and the charts example.

Fixed

  • A long BulletList row ran off both edges of the frame. Rows now wrap inside 70 % of the frame width, start right of the mark, and take the height they need. Short lists look as before.
  • check pointed at the component's own source for nodes a component adds. It now names the line of your add call.

Added

  • oxframe inspect lists each shader node's numeric parameters (amp, wetness, …) and the strength and speed of an effect, under params.
  • Guide lessons 11 to 13 as examples: scenes and transitions, sound and voice, shaders and effects.
  • The ocean example: the target scene of hybrid rendering.

Fixed

  • check reported dead_time while a shader parameter or an effect was animating, such as a growing wave or a wetting lens. Those changes now count as motion.

Shaders can read what is already drawn. A lens gets wet over the frame, a node ripples, and a scene gives way through rising water. All three run on the CPU, so check and a render without a GPU paint them, and the GPU renderer draws the same picture.

Added

  • shaders::lens_drops() puts drops on the lens over everything drawn before it, inside its box. Add it last and make it .fullscreen(). .wetness() is a signal from 0 (dry) to 1, so lens.wetness().to(1.0, 0.4) is a splash. .seed() places the drops and .drop_size() scales them. .input("scene", Input::frame()) names what it reads; Input::backdrop() is the same outside a layer.
  • Node::effect runs a shader on a node's own pixels, children included. shaders::ripple() sends rings out from the node's center: .strength() and .speed() are signals on the returned Effect. The outline stays, so use it on text, a gradient, an image or water.
  • Transition::shader paints a transition with a shader preset. shaders::water_wipe() raises a wavy waterline over the frame; below it is the next scene, rippled near the line. .wave() sets the wave height.
  • check reports input_cycle (an error) when a shader would read pixels that are not finished: lens_drops or an effect inside a group with opacity below 1, a blur, a clip, a blend, a shadow or another effect. The shader is skipped there. A misspelled input or lens_drops parameter is param_unknown with the right name.
  • inspect --graph shows effect passes with the shader that runs, and inspect names the preset of each shader node.
  • Svg::new().width() and .height() take pct(), read when the node is added. A Shader handle converts to Node, so Camera::center_on works on water.

Fixed

  • Renderers kept every image they had drawn. A waves node paints a new image each frame, so a long render grew without bound. They now keep only the images of the current frame.
  • A shader wider than the safe area (water to the edges) is no longer an out_of_frame warning, and lens_drops over text is not covers_text.

Not in this version

Input::node, Input::image and .offscreen() from the roadmap are not built. A custom WGSL shade is still checked, not run. low_contrast does not read shader pixels yet.

Breaking

  • A renderer of your own needs render_list, which draws a part of the draw list. Before → after:

// before fn render(&mut self, graph: &SceneGraph, o: &RenderOptions) -> Image { draw(&graph.draw_list(), o) } // after fn render(&mut self, graph: &SceneGraph, o: &RenderOptions) -> Image { self.render_list(graph, &graph.draw_list(), o) } fn render_list(&mut self, _: &SceneGraph, items: &[DrawItem], o: &RenderOptions) -> Image { draw(items, o) }

  • The draw list has three markers, ReadFrame, BeginEffect and EndEffect. A renderer skips them (Primitive::is_marker on docs.rs); the engine handles them.
  • The pass and inspect node structs have a new shader field.

Fixed

  • The waves example stopped with "unreachable executed" in the browser playground. The timer that reports a slow shader read the clock, and the clock panics in WebAssembly. It is now skipped there, so the example plays. Native builds, oxframe dev and the CLI were not affected, so there is no new CLI release.

A scene can paint a wave as a node. The preset renders in a check with no GPU, and the same image is what the GPU draws.

Added

  • shaders::waves() is a box in the scene. .amp(), .deep() and .foam() are signals, and a theme role such as Accent follows the theme. .uniform() sets a numeric field of your own shader.
  • Shader::source keeps WGSL in the scene. Shader::file reads it on every draw, so saving the file updates the picture without a rebuild. The text defines Params and shade. oxframe adds ShadeIn. A wrong name or type fails the check and lists the fields. WGSL that does not compile fails it too, with the line in your source.
  • A check paints shader layers at half resolution. An opaque shader over text is a warning. A pass over the draft budget is a warning.

A scene can wait for one word of a spoken line. Without a provider the length is a speech-rate estimate, so the playground and CI still run.

Added

  • Project::tts speaks through a TtsProvider. The key stays in the provider. A failed call falls back to the estimate and the scene still runs. voice("one two").start() starts the line. .at_word() waits until that word. Awaiting the line waits until the end. A line is .priority(), so it ducks a soundtrack built with .duck_under_voice().
  • The recording is cached under tts/ next to the scene. Commit that folder to render in CI without a key. Without a provider, oxframe reads a committed cache and otherwise estimates the length.
  • oxframe render --subtitles out.srt writes the lines. A path ending in .vtt writes WebVTT. --no-audio still writes them, and --range shifts the cues into that part of the video.

Sound effects mix with the soundtrack into one track. ffmpeg only encodes that mix, so the samples do not depend on the ffmpeg version.

Added

  • Audio::track builds the soundtrack. Project::audio("music.mp3") still works. .volume(), .fade_in(), .fade_out() and .master_fade() shape it. .duck_under_voice() lowers it under a clip marked .priority().
  • sound("click.wav") starts at the current frame. .play() does not wait. Awaiting it waits until the clip ends. .trim() plays a slice of the file, which is also how long the wait is.
  • The editor draws each effect on the timeline and plays the mix while you play or seek. --no-audio leaves effects out. --range keeps only the effects inside that part of the video.

A frame's draw list is a pass graph, and a layer whose vectors did not change is reused (ROADMAP task 15, stage 2). No new scene API and no shaders.

Added

  • Render passes in topological order: one vector pass when nothing opens a layer, then a composite pass for a group opacity, a blend, a blur, a shadow or a clip. Contents run before the composite that uses them.
  • A static layer is cached as the pixmap from before composite, so the next frame skips redrawing that layer. The root vector pass is not hashed, and a layer that moved or changed is drawn again. CPU bytes stay the reference.
  • inspect --graph adds a passes array (kind, node, name, items, depth, opacity, blend, filtered). Without the flag the JSON is unchanged.

A node can draw its own geometry, and a spray keeps a seeded simulation (ROADMAP task 15, stage 1). No shaders yet.

Added

  • Custom::new(|ctx, t| { ... }). ctx.line, ctx.circle, ctx.rect and ctx.path take .fill or .stroke. ctx.rng(seed) does not advance random(), and the same seed draws the same shapes after a seek.
  • Particles::new().seed(7).gravity(900.0).toward_camera() and burst(origin, count).await. Integration uses a fixed 1/120 s step and a checkpoint every 30 steps, so seeking back replays at most that many steps and lands on the same dots. toward_camera only scales the dots.
  • oxframe check reports nondeterministic when painting the same frame twice does not match.
  • Example spray: rain from Custom, then a burst into the camera.

Scenes can blend into each other (ROADMAP task 5).

Added

  • transition(Transition::slide(Dir::Left)).await at the start of a scene. Also fade, wipe, zoom_in, zoom_out, .duration, .ease, .overlap, and Transition::custom. The length is stored in meta.json and can be dragged on the timeline. render --scene leaves the incoming blend out. check samples it and inspect reports kind and progress.
  • Example transitions: a title card slides into an end card.
  • The browser presents a transition as one canvas frame. Both layers are drawn first, then blended.

Code edits itself (ROADMAP task 2). Txt still types its text out. SVG files become ordinary nodes (ROADMAP task 3).

Added

  • code.code().to(next, seconds) diffs the two sources. Tokens that stay slide to their new places, deleted tokens fade and collapse, new tokens fade in. Lines below the edit shift. Highlighting stays on the six languages and is taken from each side, not from a half-typed string.
  • insert(line, col, text, seconds), remove(((line, col), (line, col)), seconds) and replace(range, text, seconds). Lines are 1-based, columns are 0-based characters, and the range is half-open. .flash() on that tween lights the inserted text for a moment.
  • A focus on lines that move rides with them and lands on their new numbers when the tween ends.
  • Example code_steps: a function written in a few edits.
  • Svg loads a file (.src(include_bytes!(..)) or .file(path)) and expands it into groups, paths and images. .width / .height keep the aspect ratio. svg.find("id") is the element with that id, svg.paths() is every contour in paint order, and those paths morph through data like a path written by hand. Filters, masks and clip paths are skipped with a warning.
  • Example svg: a logo drawn on path by path, then one part recolored.

Breaking

  • code.code() is no longer a Signal<String>. .get(), .set() and .bind() still work. .to() is a diff, not a typewriter:
// before — `code()` was a Signal<String>, and `.to()` typed the text
let src: Signal<String> = code.code();
src.to(next, 1.0).await;

// after — `.to()` slides tokens; `.get()` / `.set()` / `.bind()` remain
code.code().to(next, 1.0).await;
code.insert(2, 0, "    let y = x * 2;\n", 0.6).flash().await;

Added

  • Camera (ROADMAP task 1): a node that zooms, pans and turns the view of everything added to it. Signals x/y (the point it looks at), zoom, rotation; center_on(node, s), fit(node, padding, s) (measures the node when called, so a growing layout fits at its current size) and reset(s). Follow a moving node with cam.x().bind(..). Nodes added to the view stay on screen (titles, captions, a HUD).
  • Zoomed content is drawn at the final scale on both renderers: text and outlines stay sharp at ×10, blurs and shadows scale with the zoom (golden frames camera_zoom, camera_rotate_blur; GPU within ΔE 0.04).
  • oxframe check does not report out_of_frame for nodes seen through a camera (framing a detail is the point); inspect marks them in_camera.
  • Example camera: a tour of a system diagram.

Changed

  • Signal::to takes anything that converts into the value: theme tokens (rect.fill().to(Accent, 0.3)), integers for f64, &str for text.

Breaking

  • An explicit .into() in .to(..) is now ambiguous; drop it:
// before
title.text().to("Hello".into(), 1.0).await;
// after
title.text().to("Hello", 1.0).await;

Scene code without Rust plumbing (ROADMAP task 4): no Box::pin, no BoxFuture in a typical scene.

Added

  • stagger(delay, items, |x| animation): the same animation on many items, each starting delay seconds after the previous one.
  • all(..) takes a Vec, an array or an iterator of animations of one kind as well as a tuple: all(cards.iter().map(|c| c.fade_in())).
  • any(..): completes when the first animation does (returns its index); the others stop where they are.
  • repeat(n, || animation) and loop_while(|| condition, || animation).
  • Node helpers, timed by the theme's motion tokens: pop_in() (scale from zero with overshoot), slide_in(Side::Left) (slides in and fades in), draw_on() (outline drawn from start to end), next to the existing fade_in() / fade_out().
  • Tween::duration(s) changes a helper's length: title.fade_in().duration(0.3).
  • Clearer compile errors: all(5), all(a, b) and a stagger closure that ends in ; explain how to fix them.

Breaking

  • sequence(delay, futures) takes any Vec, array or iterator of animations instead of Vec<BoxFuture>. Code that built the list with .collect() no longer infers its type; use stagger instead:
// before
sequence(0.15, cards.iter()
    .map(|c| -> oxframe::BoxFuture { Box::pin(c.opacity().to(1.0, 0.5)) })
    .collect()).await;
// after
stagger(0.15, &cards, |c| c.opacity().to(1.0, 0.5)).await;

Several steps per item: return an async move { … } block from the closure, no boxing.

  • all_vec(v) is deprecated: all(v) takes the Vec directly.
  • CodeExplainer::next() returns impl Future instead of BoxFuture (awaiting it is unchanged).

The first published release after 0.2.1: it also contains everything listed under 0.2.2–0.2.5 below, which were not published separately.

No crate changes. Released together with oxframe-cli 0.2.6 (oxframe mcp, --json, and hints on the compile errors agents hit most often).

The scene API and the editor protocol are unchanged.

Added

  • Crate oxframe-components, re-exported from the prelude. TitleCard, ChapterMarker, BulletList, CodeExplainer, FlowDiagram, Callout, LowerThird and EndCard are added like any other node. Each has enter, next and exit. They take color and type from the theme. LowerThird and ChapterMarker pin to the safe area. FlowDiagram lays its own nodes out in layers (.down() stacks them).
  • Node::from_id, so another crate can implement NodeBuilder.

The scene API and the editor protocol are unchanged.

Added

  • Relative placement. .next_to(other, Side::Bottom), .align_to(other, Edge::Top), .to_edge(Edge::Top) and .center_in(other) are recomputed every frame, so a node follows a neighbor that moves or resizes. The gap in next_to is the theme's Md step. to_edge pins to the safe area; a portrait frame leaves room for a vertical video's status bar and buttons.
  • .width(pct(80)) and .height(pct(50)): a fraction of the frame, or of the parent when that parent has a fixed size.
  • view.safe_area() and view.is_portrait().
  • Project::aspects([Landscape, Portrait, Square]). check lints every declared format. render --aspect 9:16 exports one; --aspect all exports each, with the shape in the file name.

The scene API and the editor protocol are unchanged. A project that does not declare aspects renders and checks at its own size, as before.

Added

  • Themes and design tokens. Project::theme(Theme::dark().accent(...)) (also light, midnight, paper, vivid) supplies colors, type roles (.display(), .h1(), .body(), .caption(), .code()), spacing (.padding(Md)), radii, shadows (.elevation(Md)) and motion (Fast/Normal/Slow, fade_in). A token is accepted wherever the concrete value is. Text with no fill uses the theme's text color. .accent(color) keeps a 4.5:1 contrast. [theme] in oxframe.toml overrides the compiled theme.
  • RELEASE.md: before a release tag, publish the crates, then move oxframe-web's playground pin to that version. The docs version list already follows crates.io; the compile image cannot.

The scene API and the editor protocol are unchanged. Existing explicit colors are unchanged. The default theme is the previous dark background and white text.

Added

  • check and inspect subcommands on the project binary (what oxframe check and oxframe inspect run). check samples the scene on the CPU, writes a storyboard and a JSON report, and fails when a node stays outside the frame, text overlaps or overflows, or text contrast is below WCAG 4.5:1. Text that flashes too briefly and a long still with no soundtrack are reported too.
  • .name("title") on every node builder. oxframe check and oxframe inspect use it; without a name the node is labeled by the add call site.

Fixed

  • The browser engine (oxframe with the wasm feature, used by the playground) did not compile in 0.2.0. CI now builds it.

Changed

  • Crate layering. oxframe-core now owns Image (RGBA pixels) and the new FrameSource trait — "give me frame *n*" — through which the editor (oxframe-preview), render/snapshot and the exporter get frames without knowing what draws them. oxframe-preview and oxframe-export no longer depend on the 2D crate or the renderers; CI checks this (scripts/check-layering.sh). Scene code is unchanged and renders byte-identically.
  • The crate docs and README carry a development-status notice.

Breaking (only for code using the internal crates directly)

  • oxframe_preview::PreviewEngine now extends oxframe_core::FrameSource: fps, size, total_frames and render moved to that trait.
// before
impl PreviewEngine for MyEngine { fn fps(&self) -> u32 { 60 } /* … */ }
// after
impl FrameSource for MyEngine { fn fps(&self) -> u32 { 60 } /* … */ }
impl PreviewEngine for MyEngine { /* the editor-specific methods */ }
  • oxframe_render::Image is a re-export of oxframe_core::Image; Image::encode_png still exists.

First release: scenes as coroutines, signals and tweens, 2D nodes with flexbox layout, text and code, effects, CPU (tiny-skia) and GPU (vello) renderers, the editor protocol, video export through ffmpeg and the in-browser (wasm) engine.
